## 1. The reconciliation question

[Issue-10 section 4](issue-10-h264-field-mbaff.md#4-capability-map-by-layer-ac-2) records the
AVD firmware command vocabulary as **unknown** for field/parity/pairing encoding: "missing
validated encoding, not proof of firmware incapability." The [project README](../../README.md)
states plainly that interlaced H.264 "is not supported by the kernel driver," and the original
reverse-engineer's README (`eiln/avd`) goes further, listing field coding under an explicit
**"Unsupported by hardware"** heading. Issue #43 asks whether the accepted design's "unknown"
classification is consistent with that stronger claim, or whether it understates the evidence.

This record does not change the "unknown at the firmware/ISA level" classification for the
*kernel's own instruction vocabulary* (`avd-inst.h`, see section 3.2). What it does is locate,
quote and date the original RE author's claim, trace how it was reached, and classify its
evidentiary weight — because "unknown" and "an named expert says no, uncited" are different
states, and the accepted design did not previously cite the second one explicitly.

## 2. The eiln/avd claim and its history

Pinned source: [`eiln/avd`](https://github.com/eiln/avd) at `e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270`,
the same revision issue-10 cites for "the original eiln/avd README."

Current README text (`README.md`, "H.264 / AVC" section):

> - Unsupported by hardware:
>   - MBAFF/PAFF interlaced. Though you will not see this unless you work in broadcast.
>   - Top/bottom field coding (x264 doesn't support)

This did not appear at project inception. Reconstructed from the file's commit history
(`git log -p README.md`, all commits by Eileen Yoon, the repository owner and sole author of
record):

| Commit | Date | What the README said about field coding |
|---|---|---|
| `9eccd0` "Initial commit" / `75ef51` | 2023-11-02 | not yet present |
| `a2ff9c`–`0bf86a` (status updates) | 2023-11-11 – 2023-11-16 | not yet present |
| `f44aad`–`003443` | 2023-11-24 | not yet present |
| `686a99` | 2023-12-01 | not yet present |
| `a5061d` "README: Update 264 asterisks" | 2023-12-04 | Top/bottom field coding listed under **"Don't know if it works in macOS"** (i.e. unverified); MBAFF/PAFF interlaced newly added to a separate, unqualified **"No:"** list, with no accompanying code change |
| `191dcf` "README: Unlock new features" | 2023-12-16 | Both items merged into a single **"Unsupported by hardware:"** heading (the current text), again with no accompanying code change to `codecs/h264.c`, `avid/h264/*.py` or any other file in the same commit |

Both reclassifications (`a5061d`, `191dcf`) are README-only diffs — `git show --stat` for each
commit lists no other file. Neither commit message nor the diff cites a trace capture, a
firmware error code, or a specific macOS sample that failed to negotiate field mode. The
public commit record does not show *when or how* the author moved from "don't know" to
"unsupported by hardware" between Dec 4 and Dec 16, 2023; it records only that they did.

**eiln/avd's public issue tracker** (issues #1–#3, the complete set at the pinned revision) was
searched for "MBAFF", "PAFF", "field" and "interlace": no matches. There is no published
discussion elaborating the claim beyond the README line itself.

## 3. What the RE author's own code implies

The README assertion is not isolated; the same conclusion is load-bearing in two places in the
author's own from-scratch reference model, which is a stronger form of evidence than a README
sentence because the code had to be written to actually decode the conformance corpus:

- `avid/h264/decoder.py` (format/geometry setup): `assert(width_mbs == (ctx.orig_width + 15) // 16)  # No interlaced`
  — the frame-geometry math is written assuming `frame_mbs_only_flag = 1` and will hard-fail
  an interlaced SPS before any decode is attempted, not just reject a specific unimplemented
  path.
- `avid/h264/rlm.py`, `init_slice()`: `raise NotImplementedError("top/bottom fields not supported by hardware.")`,
  guarded by `if (sl.field_pic_flag):` — the reference-list-management model, which reproduces
  the *hardware's* DPB/reference behavior (not just bitstream syntax), has no path for field
  pictures at all.

This is the same author, so it is not independent corroboration of the README line — but it
does show the claim is structural to their model of the hardware's reference-management
behavior, not a one-off remark. Contrast with items the same author explicitly lists as their
*own* implementation gaps rather than hardware limits (`avid/h264` "Works in macOS but not in
mine": `frame_num` gaps, multiple slice groups) — the author does distinguish "I haven't
implemented this" from "hardware can't", and places field coding in the second category both
in prose and in code.

### 3.1 What the bitstream *parser* supports (does not bear on the claim)

`codecs/h264.c`/`h264.h` (the pure bitstream/syntax parser, not the hardware model) fully parses
`field_pic_flag`, `bottom_field_flag`, `mb_adaptive_frame_field_flag`, and computes
`mbaff_frame_flag` — matching the same finding already in
[issue-10 section 4](issue-10-h264-field-mbaff.md#4-capability-map-by-layer-ac-2) for the
client/VA-API/userspace-driver layers. Parsing the syntax to know a stream needs field mode
(and reject it) is required regardless of whether the hardware can decode it; this is *not*
independent evidence about firmware capability, and issue-10 already treats it correctly as a
present-but-uninformative layer.

### 3.2 The kernel driver's own comment is not independent evidence

`drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-h264.c` at the pinned Asahi tag (`94fb233…`,
`avd_h264_validate_sps`, confirmed by direct read at this revision):

```c
if (!(sps->flags & V4L2_H264_SPS_FLAG_FRAME_MBS_ONLY))
    /* no interlaced support */
    return -EINVAL;
```

This looks like a second, independent source, but it likely is not. `git log` on this file
shows the whole driver was added in one commit, `media: apple: add avd driver` (sofus,
2026-06-30), with no reference to a specific trace or experiment in the message. The
`omarchy-m1-video` and `libva-v4l2_request` README credit "original reverse engineering in
eiln/avd" for this driver family. There is no public record establishing that the kernel
comment reflects a separately run hardware experiment rather than a restatement of the same
eiln/avd conclusion during porting. Treat it as the same claim propagated, not a second
witness, absent evidence otherwise.

Instruction-vocabulary check (answering E1 directly): `avd-inst.h` at the same tag defines the
reference-picture command word (`AVD_OP_REF`) with only `AVD_REF_NUM`, `AVD_REF_FLAG_CONST`,
`AVD_REF_FLAG_LONG` and `AVD_REF_DELTA_POC` (a single POC delta per reference) — no parity/field
bit, no second POC, no pairing field. Every other `FIELD_PREP`-named symbol in the file is the
kernel bitfield macro, not a video field-picture bit. This is consistent with, and adds no new
information beyond, issue-10 section 9.1's existing citation of `stream_refs` deriving every
reference POC delta from `top_field_order_cnt` alone. No previously-unmapped field/parity
encoding was found in the published command vocabulary.

## 4. Evidence classification table

| Claim | Classification | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| AVD firmware command vocabulary (`avd-inst.h`) has no field-parity/pairing bit | **source-observed** | direct read of `avd-inst.h` at `94fb233…`, section 3.2 above; matches issue-10 §9.1 |
| Kernel driver rejects any SPS with `!FRAME_MBS_ONLY` at `STREAMON` | **source-observed** | direct read of `avd-h264.c` `avd_h264_validate_sps`, section 3.2 above |
| "Unsupported by hardware: MBAFF/PAFF interlaced, top/bottom field coding" | **reported by original reverse engineer, uncited within the repo** | `eiln/avd` README, commits `a5061d`/`191dcf`, section 2; no linked trace, firmware error, or sample |
| eiln's own hardware/reference-list model (`rlm.py`, `decoder.py`) has no field-picture code path and assumes frame-only geometry | **source-observed**, and consistent with the README claim | direct read of `avid/h264/{decoder,rlm}.py`, section 3 above — same author, not independent of the README claim |
| Kernel driver's `/* no interlaced support */` comment is independent confirmation, separate from eiln's finding | **unresolved / no public record either way** | no citation in the introducing commit; ecosystem credits eiln for the underlying RE, section 3.2 |
| Client (FFmpeg), VA-API contract, V4L2 UAPI and userspace VA driver all carry full field/PAFF/MBAFF syntax | **source-observed** | already established in issue-10 §4/§9.2–9.4; re-confirmed here only for the bitstream-parser layer (§3.1), unchanged |
| Whether Apple's firmware itself (as opposed to every RE'd model of it) can decode field pictures | **unknown** | no public trace, firmware disassembly, or hardware experiment establishes this either way; unchanged from issue-10 |

No claim in this table is invented, and no field/parity encoding is asserted where none was
found; per the ticket's instruction, the absence of a known command is reported as absence in
the published vocabulary, not reinterpreted as proof the silicon cannot do it.

## 5. Reconciliation and decision

The accepted design's "unknown... not proof of firmware incapability" wording is defensible at
the ISA/firmware level and is not overturned here: no public source, including eiln/avd's own
model, contains a traced firmware command, error code, or capability register that directly
demonstrates the AVD coprocessor rejects field mode in hardware. The claim's true status is
**"unsupported by hardware," reported once by the original reverse engineer without a cited
trace, and structurally assumed throughout that author's own reference model** — meaningfully
stronger than "no information," but short of "independently measured." Issue-10 (and by
extension the design #14 depends on) should cite this claim explicitly by name and source
rather than leaving the firmware layer as bare "unknown," since a named domain expert's
uncited claim and total silence are not the same evidentiary state and readers of #14 should
see the distinction.

This record makes **no promise of recovering the 49 failing Main-profile vectors** and does not
change the C1 gap classification, the kernel rejection, or #14's blocked status.

## 6. What could discriminate "unsupported hardware" from "unimplemented driver support"

Per the ticket's scope, this section identifies what evidence or authorized experiment would
close the gap, without running any of it:

- **No further public record exists to mine.** eiln/avd's repository, its 3-issue tracker, and
  commit history (section 2) are exhausted; no trace dumps, firmware disassembly, or discussion
  of field/MBAFF are published anywhere in that repository. This ticket's scope excludes
  contacting the original author, so this path stops here.
- **The only remaining discriminating evidence is a kernel-side hardware experiment**, exactly
  as issue-10 already scopes in E2 ("relax `validate_sps`, correct height, field-parity POC
  deltas; decode a field-coded vector through the guard") and E3 (reference-pairing behavior).
  Both require `needs:kernel-approval`, owner consent, the lab host and the hardware guard —
  unchanged from issue-10's experiment plan; this record adds no new authorization and runs
  none of it.
- A well-supported **stop** is an acceptable outcome per the ticket, but is not recommended
  here: because the strongest available evidence is a single, uncited, non-independent source
  (sections 2–3), E2/E3 remain the only way to convert "very likely unsupported" into either a
  confirmed negative or a positive result. Recommend #14 stay blocked on E2/E3 exactly as
  issue-10 already scopes them, now citing this record for why the firmware layer is treated as
  strongly (not just nominally) unlikely to support field pictures.

## 7. Tests not run / limitations

- No hardware decode, kernel build, module load, firmware trace capture, or installation.
  Entirely source/history analysis, run on macOS.
- Git history reconstruction (section 2) relies on the public commit log of `eiln/avd`; it
  cannot see any private notes, direct messages, or unpublished traces the author may hold.
- `avd-inst.h` and `avd-h264.c` were read at the exact pinned revisions issue-10 already cites
  (`94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea`); this record re-derives the `AVD_OP_REF` and
  `avd_h264_validate_sps` citations independently as a spot check and finds them consistent
  with issue-10 §9.1, not new findings.
- This record does not re-run or extend `tests/h264-interlace-scan.py` or the 135-vector
  classification in issue-10 §9.6; those are unchanged and out of scope here.
